baseline_models.focus_anchor: The paired constructions "do not take ... awliya" and "whoever takes them in wilaya" make the relation an object of deliberate adoption.
baseline_models.mechanism: Taking/acquiring installs a wilaya relation whose live range includes close attachment, support, and standing over affairs. The noun is repeated and then converted into the subject's act, so the warning concerns chosen dependence or delegated patronage rather than mere coexistence.

activation_trace.role: The image of making or acquiring something for oneself makes the patronal relation an installed choice.
Standing over and managing an affair supplies the governing or custodial side of the adopted relation.
Love, aid, and alliance supply the supportive side of wilaya without reducing it to private sentiment.

changed_reading.before: A general ban on friendly feeling toward the two named communities.
changed_reading.after: A ban on deliberately installing their communal actors or networks as patrons, governing allies, or decisive supports.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The reciprocal "some of them are awliya of some" is followed by "whoever ... among you is from them."
baseline_models.mechanism: Repeated part-to-part language depicts an internally reciprocal network. Wilaya closes the gap between its members and runs continuously through them; entering that relation changes the operative bloc to which the entrant belongs.

activation_trace.role: The part or segment image makes the two reciprocal slots components of a larger alliance arrangement.
Nearness without an intervening gap explains how patronage creates operative adjacency and belonging.
Unbroken succession turns isolated ties into a relay-like network that persists from member to member.

changed_reading.before: "From them" names an already fixed identity.
changed_reading.after: "From them" can name an enacted affiliation: reciprocal patronage composes a bloc, and volunteering into its chain effects practical membership.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Believers are addressed before the adopted wilaya, and the ayah closes by denying guidance to the wrongdoing people.
baseline_models.mechanism: Faith carries security and trust; guidance carries course and direction; wrongdoing can be putting something outside its proper place. Taken together, the prohibited relation misallocates governing trust and thereby bends a collective course.

activation_trace.role: Settled security and trust make the addressees' search for an alternate protective center a live tension.
Direction, course, and habitual way make denied guidance the consequence of a wrongly oriented alliance.
A supporting framework or means of subsistence gives the named people a collective-system dimension.
Putting a thing outside its proper place casts the patronal transfer as a misplacement of trust and authority.

changed_reading.before: The closing non-guidance is a separate judgment appended to an identity rule.
changed_reading.after: The closing judgment diagnoses the mechanism: adopted patronage relocates security and direction, producing a collectively misoriented order.

context_deltas.mechanism: The early pericope counter-scales the focus ayah's reciprocal parts with one life repeatedly valued as all people. This revises bloc membership into an ethical danger when protection of one's part licenses destruction or corruption against the human whole.

activation_trace.role: Partition into reciprocal segments supplies the focus-side pressure toward factional partiality.
Mutual aid and alliance provide the mechanism by which a part can protect its own.
Taking life supplies the concrete terminal harm against which factional protection is measured.
Departure from sound order broadens the harm from a single act to corruption of the common field.
Wholeness without remainder makes every individual life answer to an all-people scale rather than a partisan one.
Preserving life and refraining from killing supplies the positive constraint on alliance behavior.

structural_cues: 5:51 repeats part-to-part reciprocity, while 5:32 repeats one-life/all-people equivalence around killing and saving.
The Cain sequence begins with brotherhood but shows that close relation alone does not secure justice.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies reciprocal parts and an all-human valuation of life; I infer that unjust wilaya is especially the solidarity that lets a part outrank that whole. A live alternative is that 5:32 constrains violence only and does not define patronage generally.

changed_reading.before: Reciprocal in-group support is intrinsically the whole problem.
changed_reading.after: The sharper danger is partisan patronage that makes reciprocal bloc protection override life, sound order, and justice owed beyond the bloc.

context_deltas.mechanism: The judicial pericope depicts words moved from their places, a conditional instruction to take only a favorable ruling, delegation of judgment, and subsequent turning away. These operations activate adopted wilaya as selective jurisdiction: a patron or judge is installed when useful and abandoned when the criterion resists.

activation_trace.role: Deliberate acquisition anchors the changed reading in the focus command against installing a relation.
Standing over an affair makes jurisdiction and governance a live dimension of awliya.
Deviation from a direction supplies the first operation in bending an authoritative criterion.
Putting something in its assigned place makes displacement of words a concrete reordering of authority.
Taking and holding the offered ruling supplies the context's conditional uptake mechanism.
Delegating arbitration supplies the act of placing an authority over a disputed affair.
Turning away after seeking judgment exposes an opportunistic reverse side of wilaya.

structural_cues: 5:41 sequences textual displacement, "if given this, take it," and warning when it is not given.
5:43 sequences seeking delegated judgment, possessing God's judgment, and then turning away.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies selective uptake and reversible adjudication; I infer an arrow from forum-shopping to the focus ayah's adopted patronage. The narrower alternative is that these verses diagnose only legal manipulation, not every form of wilaya.

changed_reading.before: Taking awliya is primarily an affective or social closeness.
changed_reading.after: Taking awliya includes transferring decisive jurisdiction to a network that can reroute judgment through selective uptake and withdrawal.

context_deltas.mechanism: Immediately before the focus, the packet holds together authoritative oversight, resistance to desire, distinct communal paths, a counterfactual single community, and competition in good. Difference is retained as a test while governing orientation remains answerable to revelation; the ban therefore targets transfer of criterion and allegiance, not the bare existence of plural communities.

activation_trace.role: Turning one's face, following, and approving supplies the focus-side transfer of governing orientation.
Witnessing oversight supplies a criterion that can supervise rather than erase prior communities.
The self's inclination supplies the rival directional force that can pull judgment off criterion.
A clear, manifest path makes differentiated communal routing explicit rather than accidental.
A community as a gathered type supplies the plural collective units under discussion.
Union into one direction supplies the unrealized alternative against which plurality is purposeful.
Advancing through competition converts communal difference into forward ethical action.
Inclination toward beneficial good supplies the field in which communities are told to compete.

structural_cues: 5:44 and 5:46 call the Torah and Gospel sites of guidance and light before 5:51 names their communities.
5:48 says each has a law and clear path, declines the single-community counterfactual, names testing, and commands competition in good.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies acknowledged revelations, plural paths, non-unification, and a common ethical race; I infer that 5:51 regulates allegiance across that plurality rather than commanding undifferentiated social erasure. The packet does not settle every ordinary intercommunal relationship.

changed_reading.before: The named communities as such are objects of an undifferentiated social separation.
changed_reading.after: Plural communities remain within the test, but believers must not transfer their governing orientation to communal patronage networks that displace their criterion.

context_deltas.mechanism: The next ayah exposes a crisis calculus: impaired hearts rush into the other network because they fear a reversal of fortune, while an opening or judgment may reverse that wager. Wilaya becomes protective hedging under anticipated power shifts.

activation_trace.role: Security and trust make fear-based outsourcing of protection the focus-side tension.
Aid and alliance provide the protective instrument sought by the fearful entrant.
Speed opposed to deliberation turns affiliation into an urgent move under perceived threat.
Fear with awe supplies the entrants' stated motive for seeking the other network.
Departure from health and balance diagnoses the internal distortion driving the rush.
Circulation of conditions supplies the imagined swing in power against which affiliation is hedged.
Opening what is closed through judgment supplies the event that exposes and reverses the hidden wager.

structural_cues: 5:52 directly follows the prohibition and explains the rush "among them" by fear of a turning calamity.
The feared reversal is answered by a possible opening or command from God and subsequent regret.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies haste, fear, cycling fortune, and a counter-opening; I infer wilaya as a security portfolio chosen for regime risk. "Opening" may be judgment, relief, or victory, but each alternative still overturns the fear-based calculation.

changed_reading.before: The prohibited tie is a stable preference for outsiders.
changed_reading.after: It is especially an opportunistic security hedge: rushing into a patronage network because anticipated power, rather than faith's trust, determines one's decisive support.

context_deltas.mechanism: Those who swore emphatically that they were with the believers are exposed through collapsed deeds. This context makes the focus's movement from "among you" to "from them" operational: enacted alignment can defeat a verbal membership claim.

activation_trace.role: Turning toward, following, and approving supplies the enacted orientation by which belonging changes.
The oath image supplies the strongest verbal claim of being with the believers.
Descent and collapse make the oath's apparent membership fail under exposure.
Intentional action supplies the behavioral register on which the claimed affiliation is tested.

structural_cues: 5:51 says a person can begin "among you" yet become "from them" through tawalli.
5:53 contrasts maximal oaths of being "with you" with deeds that come to nothing.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies opposed membership markers: an oath of being with one group and actions that collapse, beside tawalli that makes one from another group. I infer that operative allegiance outranks self-description; the alternative is that 5:53 concerns a particular hidden cohort only.

changed_reading.before: Communal belonging is secured by profession or declared association.
changed_reading.after: Belonging is tested by the support structure one actually enters: oath and label can say "with you" while tawalli and action make one operationally "from them."

context_deltas.mechanism: The closing pair supplies a positive counter-network: the singular wali relation is assigned to God, the messenger, and practicing believers, then tawalli yields a party organized around God. Prayer, giving, and humility make wilaya embodied practice; party and prevailing power make it collective alignment.

activation_trace.role: The focus branch of aid, affection, and alliance is the relation positively reassigned by the closing ayat.
Standing over and caring for an affair makes the singular positive wali a locus of authority and protection.
Purification and soundness make material giving a visible practice of the counter-wilaya.
Humility and lowered posture prevent the positive alliance from being defined by domination alone.
Actively entering support and alliance converts the positive wali list into a chosen affiliation.
A group organized around a shared position gives tawalli an explicit coalition form.
Prevailing force supplies the collective efficacy promised to this differently ordered alliance.

structural_cues: 5:54 profiles the replacement people by reciprocal love, gentleness toward believers, firmness, striving, and freedom from blame-fear.
5:55 uses an exclusive positive wali construction; 5:56 repeats tawalli and immediately names the resulting party.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the positive wali list, embodied practices, and party outcome; I infer that 5:51 regulates coalition architecture rather than private emotion alone. A live alternative is that the positive construction foregrounds spiritual loyalty without exhausting wilaya's political range.

changed_reading.before: The ayah only removes a relationship and leaves a social vacuum.
changed_reading.after: It redirects patronage into a worshiping, giving, humble, and mutually supporting coalition whose operative center is God, the messenger, and believers.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because the cited form is a lexicalized community name, not an instruction to derive its members' function from the root. It remains anchored because the packet supplies the name under the aid root beside awliya's aid branch. Render only as a root-image echo: the attraction of available help may intensify the temptation to promote helpers into decisive patrons.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The proper name al-Nasara stands immediately before awliya in the prohibition.

activation_trace.role: Aid and making another prevail create an exploratory helper-image inside the community name.
Aid and alliance in awliya turn the adjacent helper-image into a temptation to elevate assistance into patronage.

changed_reading.before: The named community and the patronage term contribute unrelated lexical material.
changed_reading.after: As a contained root echo, the verse may expose how the promise of help itself draws a believer toward converting helpers into governing allies.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is a form-distant activation from the packet's alternate mapped root for h-d-y. It remains anchored to the closing hidaya, qawm, and wrongdoing sequence and forms a coherent support-placement mechanism. Downstream prose must mark it as a cross-map structural image, not as the lexical meaning of "guide": misplaced patronage removes the right supports and leaves the collective order exposed to breaking.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The closing sequence denies hidaya to the wrongdoing qawm after the patronage transfer.

activation_trace.role: Severe breaking or demolition supplies an exploratory negative image behind the denial of guidance.
A supporting framework or mainstay gives the people a structure capable of standing or failing.
Misplacing something supplies the destabilizing act that leaves the collective support system wrongly assembled.

changed_reading.before: Non-guidance is only an epistemic failure to receive direction.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, it also images non-stabilization: a people who misplace patronal supports are not carried into a sound course and their collective frame remains liable to break.

strongest_changes: The focus-only friendship reading shifted to deliberate transfer of patronal, supportive, and jurisdictional alignment.
5:41-50 made selective judgment and governing criterion central while intentional communal plurality constrained an undifferentiated separation reading.
5:52 identified fear of changing power as the immediate motive for rushing into the prohibited network.
5:53-56 made belonging operational: deeds can defeat an oath, while positive tawalli produces an embodied coalition.
summary.what_was_special: The trace turned on repeated relational grammar: take awliya, reciprocal part-to-part wilaya, become from them, then a positive wali and party. The context exposed both the hidden risk calculus behind entry and the practices that constitute the counter-network.
remaining_uncertainties: The packet keeps proximity, affection, aid, governance, and coalition live within wilaya but does not select one exhaustive English equivalent.
The plural-path context limits a blanket exclusion reading without fully specifying every ordinary social relation.
The Nasara aid echo and the h-d-d collapse image are deliberately contained branch-distant activations, not lexical conclusions.
